Pool Radar: live DEX pools, cross-checked

A pool page that shows a price tells you almost nothing. What matters is depth at your size, the fee tier, what the impact curve looks like — and whether the number in front of you agrees with a second source.

Last verified 16 September 2026 · written by the DexLadder team

Two witnesses, not one feed

Pool Radar reads live pool data and cross-checks it against a second independent source on the same pool. When the two disagree, that disagreement is shown rather than averaged away. This is deliberate: a single feed that goes stale or wrong is indistinguishable from a market that moved, and in thin pools the difference is the entire trade.

What it surfaces per pool

  • Reserves and depth — the number that decides whether your size is tradable.
  • Fee tier — a 1% pool and a 0.05% pool are different instruments.
  • Price impact at real sizes — computed from the curve, not assumed.
  • Token safety checks — contract-level red flags on the base token, because a pool with perfect depth is worthless if the token cannot be sold.

Read it before you trade, not after

The habit worth building: find the pool, read depth within half a percent, compute impact for your intended size in the price impact calculator, and only then decide the order — and the tolerance. Wide tolerance on a thin pool is what makes an ordinary swap worth sandwiching.

Depth is a moment, not a property

The same pool is deep at one hour and hollow at another, deep in calm and hollow in the exact minute you need to exit. A screenshot of good depth taken yesterday is not evidence about today, which is why the radar reads live and shows the impact curve rather than a single headline number. Judge a pool at the size you actually intend to trade, in the conditions you intend to trade it.

Fee tier changes the instrument

Two pools on the same pair with different fee tiers behave differently for both sides of the market: the cheaper tier usually holds the flow, the expensive tier often holds the depth, and for a liquidity provider the fee income and the impermanent loss land in completely different proportions. Comparing pools by TVL alone hides all of it.

Keyless by construction

Everything here is read from public sources. No wallet is connected, no address is required, nothing is signed and no key exists in the product. You can scan a pool, model an order against it and walk away having authorised nothing.

Questions people actually ask

Do I need to connect a wallet to scan pools?

No. Pool Radar reads public on-chain and market data. There is no wallet connection anywhere in DexLadder.

Why cross-check two data sources?

Because a single feed that is stale or wrong looks exactly like a market that moved. Showing the disagreement is more useful than hiding it.

Does it check token safety?

It surfaces contract-level red flags on the base token alongside the pool metrics — depth is meaningless if the token cannot be sold.

Open the desk — free, no account — no account, nothing to install

DexLadder is a free, keyless gateway to Web3 — live on-chain markets, real AMM mechanics, derivatives, strategy bots and your own contracts. No account, no wallet connection, no key ever requested. Capital in the trading desk is simulated, so nothing can be deposited, withdrawn or lost, and everything stays on your device.
